author: Chris Cooley
name: Sherman Bytes
description: Deploy an M4-inspired pixel tank onto a live webpage. Breach fortified button bases, build your own cover, and hold the page against escalating squads.
controls: WASD / arrows — drive; mouse — aim the turret
Click / Space — fire; keyboard-only aiming follows the hull
B — cover (2 scrap) · T — pillbox (8) · M — mine (3)
P — pause · G — next hostile base · Esc — Recall

chapters.title: The terrain is the typography.
chapters.body: Letters block tanks and shells. Direct hits clear nearby glyphs into faint binary rubble, opening a crater wider than your tank. Whitespace becomes a route between positions. Explicit data-sherman-wall elements remain solid cover; both movement and shell rays respect their cached rectangles.

chapters.title: Breach the walls. Capture the button.
chapters.body: Four destructible wall segments surround each visible button base. Blast a gap, disable the button, and occupy it for 0.7 seconds to capture it. Friendly bases repair 18 armor per second, fire at nearby enemies, and supply one scrap every 2.5 seconds while occupied. Capturing all factories moves siege reinforcements to the page edges.

chapters.title: A tiny engineer. Your own defensive line.
chapters.body: Aim at clear ground and press B for cover (2 scrap), T for a pillbox (8), or M for a mine (3). A pixel engineer completes one job in 0.65 seconds. Cover and pillboxes sit 52 pixels ahead of the turret; mines deploy 120 pixels ahead to catch approaching tanks. Blocked construction refunds its cost. Pillboxes lead moving targets; mines deal area damage to enemy tanks.

chapters.title: The next wave is already coming.
chapters.body: Siege starts with a four-second preparation window and a ten-tank first wave. Squads arrive in groups of up to three. Later waves introduce more tanks and heavier armor, with at most 40 enemies per wave and 32 alive at once. Clear a wave for eight seconds to fortify, four scrap, and 12 armor. Conquest mode retains the original capture-every-base victory condition.

chapters.title: Salvage makes every shot count.
chapters.body: Start with 16 scrap. Earn supplies from destroyed tanks, breached button walls, base capture, and every four letters you clear. Cannon upgrades still unlock at 20 and 60 XP. Build up to 12 cover segments, four pillboxes, and eight mines. Your own walls stop your shells too, so leave firing lanes or blast a new opening.

chapters.title: Original pixel armor. Shared foundations.
chapters.body: The original M4-inspired silhouette retains its movement, two cached tread frames, independently aiming turret, and recoil. One runtime loop drives tanks, the engineer, construction, and waves. Shells use swept collision segments; movement advances in steps of at most four pixels. A shared TypeScript wave director schedules bounded squads without timers or per-enemy DOM nodes.

engine: Shared TypeScript runtime · original single-player tank simulation
extra: Visual binary opacity is 0.32 by default and preserves original text nodes. Explicit direct-text mode writes literal binary and does not fade individual glyphs. No mutation of page structure, cloned HTML, or copied Bolo assets. Recall removes owned effects and restores eligible button styles.
